My Dad is in need of a new "mp3" player. He currently has a 2nd(?) gen iPod Nano that is working but space is really limited & is showing its age. I have moved Dad over to Lubuntu from XP last year & everything is going well, but I'm looking to get him a new audio player soon.

I'd like to see at least 4GB storage space, but prefer 8 (expandable is not required but would make on-board space a moot point). It needs to support MP3 files but Ogg support would be sweet. Of course, it must work with Linux so iPods are either off the table or less preferred. It also needs to respect file names (eg "01 Test Track" needs to list/play before "02 Awesome Track"). Finally, I'd like to spend less than $50 (used is fine). Do you all know of anything that fits these requirements?

My best judgement is to get a Sansa/Sandisk but some of the newer ones apparently don't respect track names.

My recommendation is what I have, a 5.5 gen iPod running Rockbox.

EDIT: To clarify a bit more...

Rockbox can either play audio tracks that are listed in the folder or by playlists. So, if you have your songs named "01_song_name" it will play in alphabetical order (01-99, a-z, A-Z, etc).

You can find used ones, though expensive, you could go with older versions, like the 4th gen grey scale.

Also, it doesn't require any special software. When you plug it in it will switch to disk mode and you can copy the files over with your file browser. Eject and it switches back to play mode.

It also supports most audio formats, mp3, ogg, flac, etc.

If you have the 4th gen color or 5th gen's, you also get video playback.

And they even have some games. Though rather old cell phone quality, it is possible to play the original Doom on it.
I was completely unaware of this possibility. How is Rockbox interface wise? How intuitive would you say it is?

The Rockbox interface is the best part of Rockbox because it is fully customizable. There are plenty of really good themes but you can change just about everything about the interface.

Also, there is a nice utility if you don't feel comfortable with CLI to install the firmware.

Also, it has a database feature that allows you to import itunes playlists so if you still use itunes, you can.

Also, installing Rockbox will actually make it a triple boot setup. By keeping the hold button off it will start rockbox, if you turn it on and flip the hold button it will boot into ipod, if you hold some button, i forget which one, it will attempt to load a linux image.

Marguerite Steinheil was a French woman famous for her many love affairs with important men. She became notorious when it became known that she was present at the 1899 death of President Félix Faure, who allegedly had a seizure while having sex with her in his office.

In 1908 she was suspected of the murder of her husband and stepmother who were found dead in their residence dead from suffocation. The police immediately regarded her as a suspect but had no hard evidence and made a pretense of abandoning the investigation. But Steinheil herself would not let the affair rest. She made an attempt to frame her manservant by concealing a small pearl which she said had been stolen at the time of the murder in his wallet. After that fabrication was discovered, she blamed the son of her old housekeeper but he was able to establish an alibi. She was arrested in November 1908 and the sensational trial ended in her acquittal in November of 1909, although the judge called her stories "tissues of lies".

Good for you for staying positive.

  • Car: Smaller is often cheaper, to run as well as to buy. A friend of mine just moved to france with all of his and his girlfriend's belongings fitting into a three door small family car. It can be done. And they had alot of stuff. Another friend of mine got his posessions down to a single backpack when he moved to australia, which means you could go for a two seater or a large bike (assuming you can ride one).

  • You didn't mention it, but if you're looking to save money (and you don't already) learn to cook your own food with cheapo ingredients. Stews, soups, pasta, rice, egg and cheap cuts of meat are your friend. This can depend on what supermarket is available though, to make it really work you need access to a really cheap bulk place. It can help with losing wait too, and knocks your food budget in half.

  • Excercise: It's possible to do a workout in the cab of a truck so unless your folks live in japanese micro-hotel I think it should be possible, unless noise is the issue or something. Failing that, do what I do: Use the park real early in the morning. Gym memberships are crazy expensive where I live, so I'd be inclined to avoid them.

  • Downsize property: That can be hard, and it depends what you own, but second hand bookshops, DVD/electronics stores and charity shops should get rid of alot of it. Flogging stuff on ebay can work nicely too. A friend of mine literally just photographed all the novelty crap she had and put it up on facebook before she left for canada, and her friends took most of it.

  • Pay off $3,000 in debt: If you can't get any other work, I've been told that supermarkets in the US almost always need night crew, which would also help with savings since you'd get an employee discount. If you're not paying rent and eating for cheap, then you could put a serious dent in your debt and save up moving money pretty quick. $3000 is only 10 working weeks at federal minimum wage, and you'll probably be able to get a good bit more than that. I think you should be well on track before january.

Good luck!

Hey, I'm really glad things are looking up for you!

The only things I can touch on are:

I like the idea of you being able to pay off your debts. That is good and reasonable! Even if you can only find part time work, you can always look for ways to barter to lower your living costs. What do I mean? Maybe hitch rides with people, do your grocery shopping with them in exchange for going to their house first and help them unload their shit before you go home? (I'm picturing someone with a bunch of kids and a bunch to shop for)

More people's yards on the side for $, or pull weeds, whatever. Learn a little about veggie growing from them while you're at it!

Learn canning. Water-bath canning is easiest, and you can really make quite a lot. Salsas, tomato sauce/spaghetti and jellies/fruit juices are all water-bath canned. Jellies are the cheapest thing make - maybe 3-5lbs. of fruit makes 8 jars. That is 8 Xmas/birthday gifts that people are always excited about!

Now, for working out: look up bodyweight workouts - there is a subverse for that as well!

You don't need any equipment. If you have a staircase that is even better, but if not they have stairs at parks and malls too. But the best advice I've heard about it is: you can't outrun a bad diet. You can look up your BMR(basal metabolic rate) online with your height/weight and then from there, judge what your should be eating to lose/gain as you need.

Pinterest is a really good source for healthy food, once you know what your calories should be!

I swear the website eatthismuch.com - they do have a free version too, but the paid one is $9/month, so for less than $3 a week your can have these handy grocery lists and you don't have to think - my biggest issue was buying stuff "on sale," only to never eat it all before it went bad. So I waste way less food now.

Good luck!
